text: dsh-token-live 是 DSH 网页插件，在 composer 下方的 dock 增加实时读数。它根据输入草稿估算 token 数，并显示上下文占用、会话累计 token、缓存命中比例和 DeepSeek 费用；还会按相同用量对照另一种已定价模型。费用按内置高峰与空闲价格表估算，草稿估算对中日韩字符采用单独权重。适合希望在发送前查看草稿规模、了解会话用量和比较模型费用的 DSH 网页用户。无需额外密钥或账号。

dsh-token-live adds live readouts below the DSH web composer: draft token estimates, context occupancy, session usage, cache-hit share, DeepSeek cost, and a priced-model comparison. CJK receives separate draft weighting. For DSH web users checking draft size and session costs.
想在 DSH 网页输入框下查看草稿大约有多少 token。
我想知道当前会话累计用了多少 token、缓存命中了多少。
能不能在发送前看到上下文窗口已经占用了多少？
想按 DeepSeek 价格估算这个会话花了多少钱。
我想比较同一批用量换成另一种模型会花多少钱。
Show an approximate token count for my current DSH composer draft.
I want to see session token usage, context occupancy, and estimated DeepSeek spend in the web UI.
dsh-token-live 的功能「草稿 token 估算」：按当前输入草稿估算 token，中日韩字符单独加权；随输入更新，供发送前参考。
dsh-token-live 的功能「上下文占用」：读取 contextPressure 投影，在 composer 下显示下一次请求的提示词用量与模型上下文窗口比例，并用进度条表示占用。
dsh-token-live 的功能「会话用量和费用」：根据 tokenUsage 与实际使用模型的价格，显示本会话累计计费 token、缓存命中比例及估算费用；未定价模型不显示虚构金额。
dsh-token-live 的功能「跨模型费用对照」：用当前会话相同的 token 分桶和计费时段计算另一种已定价模型的费用，并在 composer dock 展示对照读数。
想在 DSH 网页上直接查看当前模型的用量费用，不想额外配置密钥。

dsh-token-live README · dsh-token-live：[](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

Live readings under the DeepSeek Harness composer: how big the draft is, what
this session has cost, and how full the context is.

dsh-token-live README · What it shows：| Reading | Source | Moves when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Draft** `≈ N tok · M chars` | the session-scoped `input` hook (`InputState.draft`) | every keystroke |
| **Cost** `¥0.42 · ¥1.8/h` | the `tokenUsage` projection × DeepSeek's published price list | each request settles |
| **Compare** `v4-pro ¥3.81` | the same buckets × the other model's prices | each request settles |
| **Context** `used / window` + bar | the `contextPressure` projection | a provider reports usage |
| **Session** `N tok · X% cached` | the `tokenUsage` projection | each request settles |

dsh-token-live README · What it shows：The plugin adds one entry to the composer dock (`conversation.composer.dock`).
It does not replace the harness's own stats pill.

dsh-token-live README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-token-live
```

Then reload the page. The browser bundle reloads on its own when a client bundle
changes; the server-side row needs the plugin tree to re-compose, which the
profile's `patchReload: live` does on save, or a `dsh web` restart.

dsh-token-live README · The reading nothing else shows：**What this session would have cost on the other model.**

The `对照` / `vs` pill prices your exact token buckets — the same cache hits, the
same cache misses, the same output — on the costliest other model in the price
list, at the same billing tier. Hovering it lists every model in the table
against your session, with the current one marked.

dsh-token-live README · The reading nothing else shows：Why it earns its place: every other cost plugin answers *what did I spend*, and
that question already has a dozen good answers. Choosing a model is a different
question — *what would the expensive route have cost me for this exact work* —
and it is the one a price list exists to answer. On this session, flash has cost
¥1.44 and v4-pro would have cost ¥3.81 for the same tokens; that is the number
worth knowing before switching, and it costs nothing to compute from data the
browser already has.

dsh-token-live README · The reading nothing else shows：A survey of the 197 entries in the awesome-dsh-plugin **Usage & Billing**
category (2026-09-12) found **zero** that report a cross-model counterfactual for
the session in view. Several compare old and new *list prices* after a rate
change; none compare *your* usage across models.

Rendered only when both models are priced: an unpriced model shows no
comparison rather than a made-up one.

dsh-token-live README · The session tooltip explains the big number：`会话 30.7M tok` looks alarming next to a 327K context. It is not 30M tokens of
content — it is the same context sent again on every step. The session tooltip
says so, dividing cumulative billed input by the newest provider-reported prompt
size: *"cumulative billed input is about 94x the current context"*. Only one of
the 197 entries says anything comparable.
section: The session tooltip explains the big number

text:
dsh-token-live README · Why the draft counter is the interesting part：The harness reports tokens after the fact. Two things in particular are not
available anywhere in it:

- **What the composer currently holds.** During streaming the client's
  `PartialAccumulator.push()` returns `false` for usage chunks, so no live token
  figure reaches the UI at all.
- **What it will cost.** Nothing in the harness carries money: the token meter's
  "pricing" is image-token pricing, unrelated to billing.
section: Why the draft counter is the interesting part

text:
dsh-token-live README · Why the draft counter is the interesting part：The harness's own estimator is a flat four characters per token
(`dsh-token-meter`'s `CHARS_PER_TOKEN`). That underprices CJK text by two to
three times, so the draft estimate here weights dense scripts separately: about
`0.7 token/character` for CJK/Kana/Hangul/fullwidth, about `4 characters/token`
for everything else.
section: Why the draft counter is the interesting part

text:
dsh-token-live README · Cost model：Official prices, CNY per million tokens, at **peak** hours
([source](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/), effective
2026-09-10):

| Model | Cached input | Uncached input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-flash` | 0.04 | 2 | 8 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | 0.30 | 9 | 27 |

dsh-token-live README · Cost model：**Idle hours bill at exactly half.** Peak is Beijing time (UTC+8), Monday
through Friday, 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00; everything else is idle. The
plugin computes the tier from the wall clock, independent of the browser's own
time zone.

Details:

dsh-token-live README · Cost model：- The model comes from the `modelSelection` projection's `lastUsed` — the model
  that actually produced the recorded usage, not `next`.
- Cache **writes** are priced at the uncached rate, because the first send of a
  prefix is a cache miss.
- A model that is not in the table renders as `未定价` / `unpriced` rather than a
  guessed number. A wrong money figure is worse than none.
- Cumulative usage is priced at the **current** tier, so a single long session
  spanning a tier change can be off by up to 2×. The tooltip says so.
- `¥/h` is a page-local burn rate (up to 15 minutes of history); it resets on
  reload.
- Prices change. The table is a constant in `lib/client.js` with the source and
  effective date next to it.

dsh-token-live README · Design: this plugin has no host half：Everything lives in one browser bundle. `lib/index.js` is an empty Cordis plugin
that exists only so the loader row has something to resolve — it injects no
service, holds no state, registers no route, writes no file, and makes no network
call.
section: Design: this plugin has no host half

text:
dsh-token-live README · Design: this plugin has no host half：The consequence worth stating plainly: **this plugin never reads your API key.**
It cannot, because it has no host half to read it with and no way to send it
anywhere. It reads four client-visible things — three projections and the
composer draft — and nothing else.
section: Design: this plugin has no host half

text:
dsh-token-live README · Design: this plugin has no host half：That is a deliberate choice, not minimalism for its own sake. On the harness
version this was developed against (0.1.5-rc.1), routes registered by a plugin on
the web server are **not** behind the session-cookie fence: a bare
`GET /dsh-market/installed` answers `200` with no cookie at all, while `/` and
`/api/` answer `401`. So a plugin that fetches a balance on the host and serves
it over its own route exposes that response to any local process that can reach
the port — and to anything else if the server is ever bound beyond loopback.
Having no host half removes that class of exposure entirely.
section: Design: this plugin has no host half

text:
dsh-token-live README · Design: this plugin has no host half：If you want account balance and are happy with a host half that holds your key,
several plugins on the awesome-dsh-plugin list do exactly that. This one
deliberately does not.
section: Design: this plugin has no host half

text:
dsh-token-live README · Accuracy and limits：- The draft figure is an estimate; cost, context and session are not.
- The draft estimate reads high on symbol-dense content (code, JSON) and is
  closest on prose. It is a pre-send sanity check, not billing.
- The context reading is absent until a provider reports usage for the session.
- Nothing here renders a live per-token count *during* generation. Doing that
  honestly needs the streaming usage path in `dsh-client-ui-chat`, which
  discards usage chunks by design.

dsh-token-live README · Development：```sh
npm test     # offline suite: estimator, price table, tier rule, render, slot registration
npm run check  # the release guard `npm publish` runs automatically
```

`npm test` executes the real `lib/client.js` under a stub `window.__ModuleLoader__`
and a stub `react`, so it needs no browser and no DSH install. It pins:

dsh-token-live README · Development：- the CJK-weighted estimator, including where it differs from the harness's own
- the price table and the peak/idle boundary at every edge (08:59, 09:00, 11:59,
  12:00, 13:00, 14:00, 18:00, weekend)
- the counterfactual: which model is picked as the alternative, that an alias
  resolves before picking, and that an unpriced model renders no comparison
- that the session re-read multiple is omitted rather than divided by zero when
  no provider-reported prompt size exists yet
- that a partial cache hit never rounds up to a full one
- that an unpriced model says so instead of inventing a number

dsh-token-live README · Development：The browser bundle is hand-written in the client module format
(`window.__ModuleLoader__.load`), so there is no build step: `lib/client.js` in
the repository is the file that ships and the file that runs.
